planningStatus: Conceptual marketing proposals; all client, venue, chef, supplier, food-safety, permit, label, rights, price, inventory and partner details proposed/TBC.
planningDisclaimer: All budgets are non-tax planning envelopes, not supplier quotations. Scenario outcomes are directional planning assumptions only and are not revenue, attendance, sales, performance, safety or compliance guarantees.

campaigns.titleEn: Origin on the Table: Regional Ingredient Proof Pop-Up
campaigns.titleMm: မူရင်းကို စားပွဲပေါ်သို့ — ဒေသထွက်ပါဝင်ပစ္စည်း အတွေ့အကြုံပြပွဲ
campaigns.commercialTension: Consumers may enjoy a dish but lack a clear, non-exaggerated reason to choose it again when multiple F&B options feel interchangeable.
campaigns.objective: Convert taste curiosity into an opted-in tasting follow-up, product trial or client-approved purchase route.
campaigns.audience: Urban food-curious adults, local-product shoppers and invited hospitality/community stakeholders; exact audience and eligibility TBC.
campaigns.creativeTerritory: The ingredient has a place, a season and a hand behind it.
campaigns.conversionMechanism: A three-station tasting card unlocks a QR ingredient/story card and a voluntary next-step preference selection; any order, delivery or purchase destination is client-approved/TBC.
campaigns.experienceFlow: Discover one regional ingredient → observe controlled preparation → taste a small labelled portion → select a preference → opt into a follow-up only with consent.
campaigns.seasonalLogic: Evergreen cultural-discovery format; use Q4 only if the client confirms a suitable product, venue and operating date.

budgetMMK.structure: Ingredient-story, controlled tasting, bilingual labelling, food-safety operations and data-capture led.

campaigns.titleEn: The Flavour Find: Guided Shelf-to-Sip Discovery Trail
campaigns.titleMm: အရသာရှာဖွေရေး — လမ်းညွှန်ထားသော Shelf-to-Sip Discovery Trail
campaigns.commercialTension: New beverages or snack variants can be overlooked when choice overload makes shoppers default to familiar products.
campaigns.objective: Help a shopper identify one personally relevant flavour route and capture a consented re-engagement preference.
campaigns.audience: Client-defined retail visitors and adult beverage/snack shoppers; retail access and age/category rules TBC.
campaigns.creativeTerritory: Do not browse the shelf. Follow your flavour.
campaigns.conversionMechanism: A five-question flavour card issues a route token to two or three client-approved discovery points, ending in a voluntary preference capture or offer reveal.
campaigns.experienceFlow: Choose a flavour mood → receive a route token → explore short product stories → sample only where approved → choose a preferred next step.
campaigns.seasonalLogic: Suitable for a non-holiday retail window; do not schedule around a public holiday without retailer confirmation.

budgetMMK.structure: Retail-routing, small-footprint display, trained guides, approved sampling and redemption instrumentation led.

campaigns.titleEn: The 15-Minute Table: Convenience Meal Kit Experience
campaigns.titleMm: ၁၅ မိနစ် စားပွဲ — အလျင်မြန်အစားအစာ Kit အတွေ့အကြုံ
campaigns.commercialTension: Busy households may perceive convenient food as less satisfying or too difficult to fit into their own routines.
campaigns.objective: Convert a convenience concern into a client-approved trial-kit reservation or cooking-demo booking.
campaigns.audience: Time-pressed households and working adults; all product, ingredient and dietary suitability details TBC.
campaigns.creativeTerritory: A real table can begin before the day has finished.
campaigns.conversionMechanism: Visitors select a real-life meal moment, watch a timed but non-performance-guaranteed demo, and reserve a limited client-approved trial kit or demonstration slot.
campaigns.experienceFlow: Choose a meal moment → view ingredient/step card → observe a controlled demo → compare serving choices → reserve a next step.
campaigns.seasonalLogic: Suitable for September household-routine planning; exact timing remains client/venue confirmed.

budgetMMK.structure: Demo-kitchen safety, client-approved kit fulfilment, staff training and reservation/feedback workflow led.

campaigns.titleEn: The Better Break: Workplace Meal Discovery Programme
campaigns.titleMm: ပိုကောင်းတဲ့ နားချိန် — အလုပ်ခွင် Meal Discovery Programme
campaigns.format: B2B workplace tasting and procurement clinic
campaigns.commercialTension: Office meal or pantry decisions can remain price-only conversations, leaving service fit, dietary information and ordering workflow unexplored.
campaigns.objective: Move a workplace decision-maker from generic interest to a consented procurement tasting or operational scoping meeting.
campaigns.audience: Client-defined HR, operations, procurement and workplace-experience decision-makers; employer access TBC.
campaigns.creativeTerritory: A break should work as hard as the team does.
campaigns.conversionMechanism: A short preference-and-operations card produces a named tasting/scoping appointment; no catering capacity or outcome is promised at the activation.
campaigns.experienceFlow: Choose a workplace use case → review practical service cards → taste approved portions → complete a procurement priority card → book a scoping conversation.
campaigns.seasonalLogic: Suitable for September business-planning windows; workplace schedule and access approval required.

budgetMMK.structure: B2B facilitation, controlled tasting, account invitation, decision capture and follow-up design led.

campaigns.titleEn: One Dish, Many Hands: Open-Kitchen Craft Table
campaigns.titleMm: တစ်ပွဲတည်း၊ လက်များစွာ — Open-Kitchen Craft Table
campaigns.commercialTension: A food brand may have a credible making process, yet customers see only the finished dish and cannot distinguish craft from generic promotion.
campaigns.objective: Create a high-attention, client-approved waitlist, tasting-session or content-consent pathway around visible craft.
campaigns.audience: Food-interested consumers, invited media/creators and client-defined guests; chef, venue and media participation TBC.
campaigns.creativeTerritory: The making is part of the meal.
campaigns.conversionMechanism: A clearly timed demonstration ends with a question card, a controlled tasting sequence and an optional waitlist or session request.
campaigns.experienceFlow: Meet the dish story → observe selected preparation steps → ask a guided question → receive serving context → request a future client-approved seat or update.
campaigns.seasonalLogic: Proposed for late September or early October before the listed Thadingyut holidays; exact date TBC.

budgetMMK.structure: Open-kitchen staging, safety separation, demonstration talent, content rights and controlled guest-flow led.

campaigns.titleEn: The Quiet Cup: Coffee & Tea Sensory Masterclass
campaigns.titleMm: တိတ်ဆိတ်တဲ့ ခွက် — ကော်ဖီနှင့် လက်ဖက်ရည် Sensory Masterclass
campaigns.commercialTension: Coffee and tea communication can become technical or status-led, making curious newcomers reluctant to ask questions or return.
campaigns.objective: Turn guided sensory participation into an optional club/session registration or client-approved product learning route.
campaigns.audience: Adult coffee/tea-curious participants; beverage, venue, age and dietary policies TBC.
campaigns.creativeTerritory: Your taste already knows where to begin.
campaigns.conversionMechanism: A guided aroma/flavour scorecard produces a self-selected learning profile and optional registration for a future session, tasting pack or client-approved update.
campaigns.experienceFlow: Choose a sensory prompt → smell/observe → taste controlled samples → complete a scorecard → select a next learning step.
campaigns.seasonalLogic: Works as a post-Thadingyut November learning format, subject to final calendar/venue confirmation.

budgetMMK.structure: Facilitation, cupware/sensory materials, controlled servings, registration workflow and learning-content led.

campaigns.titleEn: A City of Small Tables: Neighbourhood Food Passport
campaigns.titleMm: စားပွဲငယ်များ၏ မြို့ — ရပ်ကွက်အစားအစာ Passport
campaigns.commercialTension: Independent food businesses may have distinct offers but little shared mechanism to help people discover, compare and return responsibly.
campaigns.objective: Generate transparent discovery, client-approved opt-in and measurable return routes without promising sales or partnership outcomes.
campaigns.audience: Client-approved adult visitors and participating local businesses; route, safety, access, partners and operating hours TBC.
campaigns.creativeTerritory: A good city is remembered one small table at a time.
campaigns.conversionMechanism: A digital/print passport records client-approved visits or learning moments, then offers a voluntary preference capture and future route update.
campaigns.experienceFlow: Pick a route theme → receive rules/safety guidance → visit participating points → collect approved marks → reflect on a favourite → opt in to future routes.
campaigns.seasonalLogic: Proposed for November after the listed Tazaungdaing holidays; route and local-business confirmation required.

budgetMMK.structure: Route planning, local liaison, accessibility/safety communications, passport technology and field moderation led.

campaigns.titleEn: The Shared Tray: Hosted-Table Pre-Order Activation
campaigns.titleMm: မျှဝေစားပွဲ — Hosting Pre-Order Activation
campaigns.format: Seasonal hosting pop-up and group-order conversion
campaigns.commercialTension: People planning a shared meal can lack confidence in what to order, how much to choose or how to coordinate a group without over-ordering.
campaigns.objective: Move hosting interest into a client-approved group-order consultation, menu-planning tool or pickup/delivery enquiry.
campaigns.audience: Client-defined households, office hosts and community organisers; service area and eligibility TBC.
campaigns.creativeTerritory: The table begins with the people you are thinking of.
campaigns.conversionMechanism: A table-size planner creates a non-binding hosting card and offers an optional client-approved pre-order or consultation request.
campaigns.experienceFlow: Choose a gathering moment → set a table size → explore menu/serving prompts → build a non-binding card → request the next approved service step.
campaigns.seasonalLogic: Proposed for the November–December hosting period while avoiding the listed 4 and 25 December dates unless operations are confirmed.

budgetMMK.structure: Table-set design, planner UX, client-approved menu information, lead routing and service coordination led.

campaigns.titleEn: The Buyer’s Bite: MSME Food Trade Preview
campaigns.titleMm: ဝယ်ယူသူအတွက် တစ်ကိုက် — MSME Food Trade Preview
campaigns.format: Curated B2B trade preview and buyer-meeting clinic
campaigns.commercialTension: Emerging food producers may generate interest yet lack a structured, realistic route to a buyer conversation, product review or next qualification step.
campaigns.objective: Turn selected product discovery into a client-approved buyer meeting, product-review request or category briefing—not an implied listing or endorsement.
campaigns.audience: Client-approved food buyers, distributors, hospitality/procurement leads and invited MSME producers; participant selection TBC.
campaigns.creativeTerritory: One good bite should open a better conversation.
campaigns.conversionMechanism: A structured buyer card captures criteria and issues a named, consented follow-up request after a client-approved product interaction.
campaigns.experienceFlow: Review category brief → meet selected producer/story → conduct controlled product interaction → complete buyer criteria card → request a meeting or review.
campaigns.seasonalLogic: Suitable for late November/early December category-planning windows, excluding public-holiday operations unless confirmed.

budgetMMK.structure: Buyer curation, producer readiness, controlled meeting operations, product handling and follow-up governance led.

campaigns.titleMm: ဒုတိယအကြိမ် စားသုံးမှု — Feedback-to-Return Packaging Lab
campaigns.format: Product-feedback pop-up and CRM reactivation programme
campaigns.commercialTension: A first trial may not become a repeat habit because brands often learn too little about the actual serving, storage, pack-opening or re-order friction.
campaigns.objective: Generate consented, structured feedback and a client-approved re-engagement route without claiming packaging, sustainability or compliance outcomes.
campaigns.audience: Existing client-approved customers or invited trial participants; product/category and data permissions TBC.
campaigns.creativeTerritory: The next serving begins with what the first one taught us.
campaigns.conversionMechanism: A guided pack-use review captures a priority friction and lets the participant select a future update, trial or client-approved repeat-purchase prompt.
campaigns.experienceFlow: Review an approved use moment → identify one friction → rank practical needs → receive a transparent response path → opt in or decline follow-up.
campaigns.seasonalLogic: Evergreen retention format; can run in December only around confirmed client operations and public-holiday guardrails.

budgetMMK.structure: Customer research, bilingual feedback design, CRM segmentation, client-approved response workflow and moderation led.
